title: It Is Finished! Glorious Word
description: It Is Finished! Glorious Word in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 136, “"It Is Finished."”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: It is fin-ished! glo-rious word From thy lips, our suf-fering Lord! Words of high, tri-um-phant might, Ere thy spir-it takes its flight. It is fin-ished! all is o'er; Pain and scorn op-press no more.

lines: From thy lips, our suffering Lord!
Ere thy spirit takes its flight.
It is finished! all is o'er;
Pain and scorn oppress no more.
Shades the path thy feet must tread;
No more fear, lest in thine hour
Not a stain of weakness lies.
All thy toils are now o'erpast;
Thou hast found thy rest at last;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch died in 1870.
credits: Words by Stephen Greenleaf Bulfinch (1809–1870), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
